record.paper_title: QCD, from its inception to its stubbornly unsolved problems
record.original_question: Can lattice QCD devise a gauge-invariant way to characterize a confined constituent-quark propagator that peaks at a constituent mass roughly 300 MeV larger than a Lagrangian or chiral-model mass, and can it also determine whether one-gluon-exchange dominance explains mass differences between baryons with the same quark constituency but different spin or quark-spin alignments?

evidence.quote: Presumably, if latticists could device a gauge-invariant way to characterize a confined constituent-quark propagator, it would be found to peak at a “constituent mass” some 300 MeV larger than a “Lagrangian” or chiral-model massg.
Similarly, they might discover one gluon exchange dominance for the mass differences between baryons of the same quark constituency but different spin or quark-spin alignements.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the framework of lattice quantum chromodynamics (QCD), the theory of an SU(3) gauge field coupled to quark fields with a Lagrangian (current) quark mass m_q, address the following two questions.

(a) Devise a gauge-invariant construction on the lattice of a propagator G(p) for a confined quark inside a hadron such that:
  (i) G(p) is invariant under local SU(3) gauge transformations of the quark and gluon fields;
  (ii) G(p) is well-defined and computable in pure lattice QCD (without recourse to model assumptions);
  (iii) the resulting spectral function or pole-like structure of G(p) exhibits a peak at an effective "constituent" mass M_c that exceeds the Lagrangian mass m_q (or the small chiral-model mass) by approximately 300 MeV for the light quarks (u, d).

(b) Using only first-principles lattice QCD computations, determine whether the mass splittings between baryons composed of the same quark flavor content but with different total spin or different internal quark-spin alignments (for example the N(939)–Δ(1232) splitting, or the Σ–Λ splitting) are dominantly accounted for by a single perturbative one-gluon-exchange interaction between constituent quarks (in the spirit of the De Rújula–Georgi–Glashow chromomagnetic hyperfine interaction proportional to (λ_i·λ_j)(σ_i·σ_j)/(m_i m_j)), as opposed to receiving comparable contributions from other non-perturbative or multi-gluon mechanisms.

Provide either an explicit construction and lattice measurement establishing both (a) and (b), or a proof that no such gauge-invariant constituent-quark propagator with the stated property exists, or that one-gluon-exchange dominance fails for these baryon mass splittings.
artifact.status_search_result: No gauge-invariant lattice construction of a constituent-quark propagator with a ~300 MeV mass shift over the Lagrangian mass is established in the literature; standard lattice studies of the quark propagator are performed in fixed gauges (Landau gauge), and the relation to a constituent mass remains model-dependent. Lattice studies of baryon spectroscopy reproduce N–Δ and other hyperfine splittings nonperturbatively, but a clean demonstration that one-gluon exchange alone dominates these splittings has not been given. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Lattice QCD and the constituent quark model
status_evidence.snippet: Presumably, if latticists could devise a gauge-invariant way to characterize a confined constituent-quark propagator, it would be found to peak at a constituent mass some 300 MeV larger than a Lagrangian mass.
status_evidence.claim: Open challenge to lattice QCD to provide gauge-invariant constituent-quark propagator and to test one-gluon-exchange dominance for baryon hyperfine splittings.
